item.title: Australian politics live: NSW One Nation leader clarifies anti-abortion comments; NDIA says job cuts necessary
item.author: Krishani Dhanji
item.content:encoded: Follow the day’s news liveSports precinct funding report reveals a ‘pattern of behaviour’, Wilson says says there are questions for Labor to answer over an ABC report which says health minister office asked an Adelaide council to put forward a $6m sports precinct upgrade for federal funding before any detailed costings or formal planning had been done.I think what we’re now seeing is a pattern of behaviour. The prime minister gave a grant to a golf course in his electorate just around the corner from his home, of which he was a member, which he failed to declare. Now we have the health minister, the next wannabe prime minister, doing exactly the same thing.That’s a difficult thing to do. However, I think one way to do it is to ensure that Muslim leaders are at the centre of any such discussion and guide that discussion in a way that Australian Muslims as a whole do not feel targeted.Because there is a real risk when you have a discussion about extremist Islam, you have a real risk that Muslims as a whole feel under pressure. Equally, if you don’t have that discussion, you play into the hands of extremists at the other end of the spectrum.Continue reading...

item.title: Six green card holders in Texas charged in federal crackdown on illegal voting – US politics live
item.author: Robert Mackey (now); Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
item.content:encoded: Four illegal votes were apparently counted in error out of 11,388,670 votes placed in 2024 general election in Texas, the FBI director, is now testifying before lawmakers on the Senate judiciary committee. A reminder that the last time he appeared before Congress was in May, when he sparred with senators on the appropriations committee and denied – under oath – allegations of excessive drinking and unexplained absences on the job, dismissing them as “baseless” during a fiery congressional hearing.Today’s hearing is also expected to be full of heated exchanges. “Mr Patel is the least qualified and most partisan FBI director in our nation’s history,” said Senator Dick Durbin, the judiciary committee’s top Democrat. “The bureau has been reshaped as a political weapon against President Trump’s political enemies and a shield to protect the president and his MAGA loyalists, not the American people.”Continue reading...

item.title: Anthropic’s CEO calls for AI slowdown as Nvidia’s urges acceleration
item.author: Danielle Abril
item.content:encoded: At San Francisco conference, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman calls for more rigorous security measuresAnthropic’s CEO took the stage at a conference in San Francisco on Tuesday to reiterate his call for a slowdown of AI development, while Nvidia’s CEO argued against such deceleration.Dario Amodei used an automotive analogy to make his point: when a competing car company has a safety incident like brake failures, it is a moment for all car companies to stop and review their own practices, he said at Salesforce’s Dreamforce convention on Tuesday.Continue reading...

item.title: Yvonne Whear’s car found in river as mystery surrounding NSW woman’s disappearance continues
item.author: Susan Chenery
item.content:encoded: Police say personal items thought to belong to Whear recovered from waterlogged vehicleA car belonging to missing woman Yvonne Whear has been found in northern New South Wales, about seven months since the 73-year-old was last seen.Following a tip off, police divers found the car in the Rous River in Dulguigan on Saturday, 12 September – a short distance from Whear’s home.Continue reading...

item.title: US set to deliver 2,000lb bombs to Israel as part of vast arms deal
item.author: Associated Press
item.content:encoded: Powerful bombs prompted such concern about mass deaths in Gaza that Biden officials paused delivery two years agoThe Trump administration is planning to deliver powerful 2,000lb bombs to Israel as part of an upcoming arms deal, weapons that prompted such concerns about the possibility of mass casualties in Gaza that the Biden administration paused their delivery two years ago.The $2.8bn package includes 40,000 bombs, made up of 20,000 MK-84s and 20,000 BLU-117s, according to two US officials and a person familiar with the plan who spoke on Tuesday on condition of anonymity to discuss the package, which is not yet final.Continue reading...

item.title: Queenslanders’ rights to oppose mining projects ‘gutted’ by new laws, activists say
item.author: Andrew Messenger
item.content:encoded: As minister says process needs to be ‘streamlined’, Greens and Lock the Gate say the legislation is ‘corrupt’ and tears up environmental protectionsQueenslanders’ right to object to mining projects – including coal – would be “gutted” by new legislation that would ban opponents from being heard in court without the minister’s approval and then only if they owned a property within a 125km radius of the project.The Greens have called the move “corrupt” and community action group Lock the Gate Alliance said the state’s LNP government was “tearing up democratic and environmental protections just to make life easier for mining companies”.Continue reading...

item.title: Sleeping teen and camper wounded as Colorado bear attacks reach record high
item.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
item.content:encoded: Bears came through bedroom window and swiped tent at campground, causing scratch marks and puncture woundA black bear burst through a Colorado teenage girl’s window and scratched her, days after a bear also bit a camper in the state, according to wildlife officials.On Friday, a woman at a campground in south-west Colorado heard a growl and felt something hit her outdoors tent, according to a news release.Continue reading...

item.title: Trump May Not Be Entirely Wrong About A.I.
item.author: Bret Stephens
item.content:encoded: Has A.I. become death, destroyer of worlds?

item.title: Scrutiny of Jury May Complicate Future of Lindsay Clancy Case
item.author: Jenna Russell and Nicholas Bogel-Burroughs
item.content:encoded: The intense public focus on the jurors whose deadlock led to a mistrial could complicate any attempt to retry the case, and to seat jurors in other high-profile cases.

item.title: Kennedy Center Closes Its Doors Despite a Judge’s Order
item.author: Julia Jacobs and Zach Montague
item.content:encoded: The announcement came after President Trump said he would cancel a $257 million renovation of the venue if his name is not returned to the building.

item.title: About 1,500 Britons a day quitting their jobs to become unpaid carers
item.author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
item.content:encoded: More than a million people have left work to look after loved ones in the past two years, Carers UK saysAbout 1,500 Britons a day are quitting their jobs to become unpaid carers, as they try to balance their vulnerable relatives’ growing care needs with declining access to state-funded social care services.Research estimates that more than a million people have left the workplace to look after ageing, ill and disabled loved ones in the past two years, highlighting the social challenges caused by UK’s rapidly changing demographic profile.Continue reading...

item.title: Thirteenth Met police officer sacked after undercover BBC investigation
item.author: Yassin El-Moudden
item.content:encoded: PC Mason O’Connor dismissed following Panorama film showing misogyny and racism at London police stationA 13th serving Metropolitan police officer has been dismissed in relation to an undercover BBC investigation into misogyny and racism at Charing Cross police station.PC Mason O’Connor was found to have committed discreditable conduct and breached professional behaviour standards, linked to a comment he made towards a female colleague, according to the Met.Continue reading...

item.title: Britons of all ethnicities feel racial equality is worsening, study shows
item.author: Geneva Abdul
item.content:encoded: Nearly half of minority ethnic respondents in a poll say they have faced prejudice over the past year Many Britons feel inequality is worsening and that discrimination has become more common, according to a thinktank study.The report by British Future has found that people across ethnic groups believe racial equality is worsening in Britain. One in six people are from minority ethnic backgrounds.Continue reading...

item.title: It’s Already Too Late to Stop the A.I. Threat
item.author: Thomas L. Friedman
item.content:encoded: China and the United States must work to repair the damage A.I. has done now, not look to future developments.

item.title: Mail-in disaster averted as Trump in angry froth after court defeat
item.author: Sam Levine in New York
item.content:encoded: Election officials continue push to assure Americans mail ballots are safe after supreme court rules against presidentAfter the US supreme court halted Donald Trump’s efforts to make it significantly harder to vote by mail in the midterms, US election officials are redoubling their efforts to convince Americans it is safe to cast their ballots by mail.The supreme court’s Monday ruling, which sent Trump into an angry froth on Truth Social, averted what election officials of both parties said would be an administrative disaster for this year’s elections. Trump’s order would have required states to comply with cumbersome new rules, including redesigning mail-in envelopes and uploading lists of voters to the USPS, that were not feasible to implement before ballots started going out. The effort was seen as a push by the government to change voting policy as well as one to weaken confidence in voting by mail.Continue reading...

item.title: Trump Threatens to Cancel Kennedy Center Renovation
item.author: Matthew Cullen
item.content:encoded: Also, the world is furious over rising prices. Here’s the latest at the end of Tuesday.

item.title: Iran war cost US $38bn and significantly depleted missile stockpile, report finds
item.author: Joseph Gedeon and Andrew Roth in Washington
item.content:encoded: Damaging budget report estimates cost would grow $3bn per month and stockpile could take five years to rebuildThe war in Iran has cost the US at least $38bn and left its stockpile of defensive missiles so depleted it could take five years to rebuild, the non-partisan Congressional Budget Office (CBO) has found, in a damaging report less than two months before midterm elections where the war and the cost of living crisis will likely hurt Republicans at the polls.The economic report comes a day after the Pentagon’s inspector general finally released its own first review of the war, saying that the US spent $22.3bn on munitions alone through 30 June, put total spending at $33.4bn, and found the fighting had “resulted in strategic inventory shortfalls and revealed industrial base bottlenecks for munitions resupply”.Continue reading...

item.title: Search under way for three-year-old boy missing from Suffolk playground
item.author: Yassin El-Moudden
item.content:encoded: More than 100 people reported to have joined search for Noah, who is autistic, non-verbal and has partial hearing lossPolice are urging people to check their gardens and sheds for a three-year-old boy who went missing on Tuesday during a visit to a playground near the Suffolk-Essex border.The boy, named Noah, was last seen at 3pm in Merriam Close in Brantham, near Manningtree, before being separated from a relative. Officers from Suffolk constabulary said Noah was reported to have run down an alleyway near the playground towards a housing estate.Continue reading...

item.title: Air pollution linked to higher suicide risk, international research suggests
item.author: Anna Bawden Health and social affairs correspondent
item.content:encoded: Analysis of 29 studies highlights potentially heightened danger from small particulate matter and nitrogen dioxide Environmental pollution is known to be associated with poorer mental health but its role in suicide risk is less well understood. Scientists at Queen’s University Belfast examined whether air, noise, light, and water pollution could influence the risk of death by suicide and suicidal behaviours.Continue reading...

item.title: Labor accused of throwing creatives ‘under the bus’ with proposal to ease copyright protections for AI giants
item.author: Luca Ittimani and Caitlin Cassidy
item.content:encoded: Compromise revealed as senior personnel from OpenAI, creator of ChatGPT, meets Albanese ministersThe Albanese government is considering giving AI companies access to Australian creatives’ works by default as it pursues a compromise with US tech giants.The proposals were revealed as senior personnel from OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, met with Labor ministers and warned that Australia’s copyright laws were preventing the company from training models locally.Continue reading...

item.title: A T. Rex Walked Here: Teacher Finds Rare Footprints in North Dakota
item.author: Adeel Hassan
item.content:encoded: Kent Hups, a high school science teacher in Colorado, discovered a 23-foot trackway of fossilized dinosaur footprints, which offer a glimpse of how the apex predator moved 66 million years ago.

item.title: Ferocious fight among Brazil’s supreme court erupts on eve of presidential election
item.author: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro
item.content:encoded: Scandal explodes as country’s election campaign peaks, with polls suggesting dead heat between candidatesBrazil’s supreme court has been thrust into what experts consider the greatest crisis since the return of democracy in the 1980s, as two rival judges lock horns on the eve of the presidential election with unpredictable consequences for Latin America’s largest democracy.The politically charged dispute exploded into public view on Tuesday as judges traded insults and accusations during a heated supreme court hearing that was livestreamed into millions of Brazilian homes.Continue reading...

item.title: Carney says Canada will pursue ‘unique security and economic alliance’ with EU amid US trade spat
item.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto and Jennifer Rankin in Strasbourg
item.content:encoded: Prime minister speaks of strengthening Canada’s economic and political ties to Europe at Canada Investment SummitMark Carney said Canada will pursue a “unique security and economic alliance” with Europe as he positions his country as a base to build in the “new global economic order”.Speaking to investors, company executives and government ministers at the inaugural Canada Investment Summit on Tuesday, the prime minister pitched Canada as a “safe harbour” and lucrative home for foreign capital as his government looks to reduce its reliance on trade with the United States.Continue reading...

item.title: Houthis threaten more Saudi strikes as UN warns of humanitarian crisis in Yemen
item.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
item.content:encoded: Estimated 100,000 Yemenis displaced amid renewed fighting as Qatar sounds alarm over Bab al-Mandab straitSaudi cities faced the threat of a second day of Houthi attacks as fighting across Yemen led the UN to warn of a humanitarian crisis with 100,000 Yemenis already displaced.As oil prices remained well over $100 (£74) a barrel, Qatar warned of a catastrophe if the Iran-backed Houthi militants won full control of the Bab al-Mandab strait, the narrow waterway at the bottom of the Red Sea dominating the key naval route to Asia. The strait has become vital to Saudi crude oil exports as the wider Middle East war chokes the strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.Continue reading...

item.title: Top Democrat on House oversight panel investigating Trump Jr wedding party bankrolled by Russian oligarch
item.author: Ariana Baio
item.content:encoded: Robert Garcia expresses concern over ‘any possible foreign entanglement’ between White House and Umar KremlevRobert Garcia, the top Democrat on the House oversight committee, is investigating potential ties between the White House and a Russian oligarch who paid for a portion of Donald Trump Jr’s wedding.In a letter sent to Susie Wiles, the White House chief of staff, on Monday, Garcia expressed concern about “any possible foreign entanglement” between the president’s son and the oligarch, Umar Kremlev. Garcia asked Wiles to provide documents, records and communications between the White House and Trump Jr about Kremlev, among other requests.Continue reading...

item.title: ‘This should be condemned by any thinking human’: film industry rallies behind NAZA directors
item.author: Catherine Shoard in London and Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
item.content:encoded: Backing comes after Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor were threatened with having their citizenship revoked and accused of treasonFilm industry heavyweights across the globe have expressed solidarity with Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, the Oscar-winning Israeli directors of documentary NAZA, who have been threatened with having their citizenship revoked by Israel’s culture minister, who accused them of “treason against the state”.NAZA, which was produced by the Guardian, is named for an acronym euphemistically used by Israel’s intelligence service to indicate how many civilians it expects to die in an airstrike on Gaza. It includes interviews with 24 Israeli military or intelligence soldiers and officers who outlined the AI-powered targeting systems used to bombard Gaza, resulting in the mass killing of Palestinian civilians.Continue reading...

item.title: Indonesian wildfires threaten leading orangutan research site in Borneo
item.author: Gloria Dickie
item.content:encoded: Critically endangered Bornean orangutans flee forests as staff at Cabang Panti work round the clock to stave off blazeWildfires in Indonesia are sweeping through a critical research site for Bornean orangutans and are now threatening a celebrated research camp, home to one of the world’s longest-running studies of wild apes.In the past few days, the fires have burned within 200 metres of Rangkong research station, a satellite of Cabang Panti research station, which lies about four miles north in Gunung Palung national park.Continue reading...

item.title: Russian warship fires flares at Danish helicopter as Nato jets shoot down drone over Lithuania
item.author: Jon Henley Europe correspondent
item.content:encoded: Ursula von der Leyen says incidents ‘part of broader pattern of Russian aggression and provocation against Europe’A Russian warship fired two emergency flares at a Danish helicopter in the Baltic Sea and an Italian Nato fighter jet shot down a drone carrying an explosive device over Lithuania in what the EU described as “reckless and dangerous” Russian behaviour.Poland also scrambled fighter jets “due to the activity of Russian jet-powered unmanned aerial vehicles conducting strikes on Ukrainian territory”, the day after Polish security forces retrieved a suspected Russian drone adrift in its waters.Continue reading...

item.title: Rising Fuel Prices Set Off Anger and Protests Around the World
item.author: Damien Cave
item.content:encoded: From Indonesia to Guatemala to Syria, shortages and price increases are leading to protests and blackouts.

item.title: Pauline Hanson’s daughter Lee working for a NSW One Nation senator remotely from Tasmania without ministerial approval
item.author: Sarah Martin Senior correspondent
item.content:encoded: Lee Hanson also appears to be regularly campaigning for party during work hours, social media showsPauline Hanson’s daughter, Lee Hanson, has been working in Tasmania as a senior adviser to a New South Wales One Nation senator without the required ministerial approval, Guardian Australia can reveal.Under work base arrangements that apply to the staff of all MPs, a personal adviser such as Hanson can only be allowed to work in a location other than Canberra or the parliamentarian’s home base with approval from the special minister of state.Continue reading...

item.title: Explosive device found on drone shot down in Lithuania, says minister - as it happened
item.author: Jakub Krupa (now and earlier) and Martin Belam (earlier)
item.content:encoded: The European Commission’s president warned that recent actions in Denmark and Lithuania are ‘not isolated incidents’Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha responded to the incident in Denmark, declaring Kyiv’s “full support” after “unacceptable actions targeting a Danish helicopter.”“Moscow continues its attempts to destabilise Europe, not just Denmark. Joint and decisive action is required and Ukraine is ready to contribute to all efforts aimed at strengthening the protection of Europe from Russian threats,” he said.Continue reading...

item.title: Jamie Beaton Could Be the World’s Most Educated Person
item.author: Scott Cacciola
item.content:encoded: Jamie Beaton has 12 advanced degrees from Harvard, Yale, Oxford and other top universities, with more on the way. Why? How?

item.title: UK sanctions on Israel ‘fall far short’ of its obligations, legal experts say
item.author: Haroon Siddique and Geneva Abdul
item.content:encoded: More than 130 sign letter to PM saying international law requires further measures to stop illegal settlementsMore than 130 legal experts, including 18 king’s counsel (KCs), have written to Andy Burnham saying that sanctions on Israeli settlements “fall far short” of Britain’s obligations under the international court of justice’s (ICJ’s) finding that the occupation is unlawful.Continue reading...

item.title: Jaguar Land Rover in talks to sell Defender to Nato countries
item.author: Julia Kollewe
item.content:encoded: Carmaker builds on relationship with British armed forces by seeking to cash in on Europe’s rearmament driveJaguar Land Rover is in talks with Nato countries about selling them the newly revamped Defender military vehicle, as the UK-based carmaker seeks to tap into Europe’s defence spending boom.It is also among carmakers bidding for a UK defence ministry contract worth £900m to replace an ageing fleet of Land Roversthat have been out of production since 2016, competing with General Motors and the UK’s Ineos Automotive, which builds the Grenadier 4x4 for the civilian market.Continue reading...

item.title: Imran Khan’s sons accuse Pakistani army chief of vendetta against imprisoned father
item.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi and Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad
item.content:encoded: Kasim and Sulaiman Khan tell Guardian they believe ex-PM is being ‘slowly killed’ by harsh treatment, driven by Asim MunirThe sons of Imran Khan have accused Pakistan’s powerful army chief of a “personal vendetta” against the incarcerated former prime minister and expressed fears their father is being “slowly killed” in jail, as international pressure mounts over his prison conditions.Kasim Khan, 27, and Sulaiman Khan, 29, have become strong advocates for the release of their father, who has been held in Adiala prison in Rawalpindi since his arrest in 2023, and is serving a 14-year sentence on corruption charges.Continue reading...

item.title: Venice best actress winner says she signed on at Danish job centre days before her victory
item.author: Philip Oltermann European culture editor
item.content:encoded: Mathilde Arcel, who won the Volpi Cup on Saturday for her role in Golden Lion winner Woman Unknown, said job offers have now begun to arriveThe winner of this year’s best actress prize at the Venice film festival has revealed that she is on unemployment benefits and had to fly to back to Copenhagen to report to the job centre before receiving her award.On Saturday night, Danish actor Mathilde Arcel won the prestigious Volpi Cup for her first leading role in a feature film, May el-Toukhy’s post-second world war drama Woman Unknown, which also won the Golden Lion award for best film.Continue reading...

item.title: What would it take to make India’s cities better – and safer?
item.author: Niha Masih
item.content:encoded: After a five-storey building collapsed in Delhi, focus is on how urban areas can adapt to growing populations. Plus, Ahmedabad’s ace newspaper delivery driver goes viralRecently, I may have saved a woman’s life on the road. Somehow, this was something I had expected to happen.On that day, I saw a truck leave a construction site with a tangled wire trailing behind. I frantically looked to see what the wire was attached to and spotted the scaffolding a few meters ahead. I shrieked and grabbed the hand of the woman walking in front of me just as the metal pipes came crashing down. We hugged for a brief second, and then walked our separate ways.Continue reading...

item.title: Houthis seize strategic Red Sea islands as analysts warn of impending oil crunch
item.author: Jonathan Yerushalmy
item.content:encoded: The militant group in Yemen captured the islands of Greater and Lesser Hanish, near the chokepoint of the Bab al-Mandab straitYemen’s Houthi militants have seized two strategic islands in the Red Sea, reinforcing the Iran-backed group’s ability to control a key shipping route, as concerns mount that the world is facing a new oil supply crisis.The seizure of the islands of Greater and Lesser Hanish is the latest in the militant group’s swift advance across Yemen’s Red Sea coast, after the capture of the port of Mokha and Perim island in the Bab al-Mandab strait.Continue reading...

item.title: ‘I believed the hype’: the white South Africans denied refugee status in the US
item.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
item.content:encoded: Drive to save thousands of Afrikaners from false claims of ‘white genocide’ appears to show signs of slowingWhen Donald Trump announced in February 2025 that the US would accept Afrikaners from South Africa as refugees, many white South Africans who believed that they were victims of racism in their country thought that their prayers had been answered.However, in the past few months, dozens of applicants to the refugee programme have been rejected, with many left dismayed and confused as to why they would be left to face what Trump has falsely claimed is a “white genocide” in South Africa.Continue reading...

item.title: Ebola outbreak in DRC has peaked, say authorities, as infection rates slow
item.author: Prosper Heri Ngorora in Goma
item.content:encoded: Almost 3,500 people have died in outbreak and experts say more must be done to ensure Bundibugyo is under controlAuthorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have announced that the Ebola outbreak ravaging parts of the country has reached its peak.For the first time since the epidemic was declared in May, the numbers of people becoming infected is slowing down, according to officials.Continue reading...

item.title: Panama canal traffic facing further cuts as drought from El Niño worsens
item.author: Mark Saunokonoko with Agence France-Presse
item.content:encoded: Planned daily reductions will further choke one of the world’s most important shipping lanesThe Panama canal plans to again cut maritime traffic due to worsening drought caused by the El Niño climate phenomenon, further choking up one of the world’s most important shipping lanes.The canal handles 5% of global maritime trade and about 40% of US container traffic; it is favoured by shippers because it usually reduces cost and transit times, especially for companies trading between China, Asia and the US.Continue reading...

item.title: AI-linked stocks slide after tech bosses call for slowdown in ‘reckless’ development
item.author: Lauren Almeida
item.content:encoded: Donald Trump dismisses attempts to increase controls on artificial intelligence as ‘sick conspiracy’ Shares in the semiconductor designer Nvidia – the world’s most valuable company – were down 3.3% by market closing in New York City, while Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) slid 4% and Micron Technology and Sandisk shares slumped by 5%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq index fund was down 0.5% by the end of the day.Continue reading...

item.title: Do You Have Questions About A.I.? We Want to Answer Them.
item.author: Cade Metz
item.content:encoded: The New York Times is soliciting readers’ questions about the dangers — and benefits — posed by artificial intelligence.

item.title: ‘A coin flip’: on the campaign trail as Brazil’s far right edges back to power
item.author: Tom Phillips in Juiz de Fora
item.content:encoded: Neck-and-neck with Lula in polls, Flávio Bolsonaro fires up his base in the bellwether state of Minas Gerais – starting at the scene of his father’s stabbingA giant banner of Brazil’s incarcerated former president Jair Bolsonaro fluttered in the morning breeze as his eldest son, Flávio, touched down at an airfield on the fringe of a city that will soon help decide the future of one of the biggest democracies on earth.“Brazil is rudderless. Brazil has no president and Brazil needs a president – and that president is Flávio Bolsonaro,” the far-right senator declared as he waded into the flock of supporters who had gathered to welcome him to Juiz de Fora, one of the largest cities in the battleground state of Minas Gerais.Continue reading...

item.title: The London hospital funded by donors who invested in the slave trade
item.author: Written by Morgan Ofori and David Conn; Animation by Alexander Purcell; Photography by Wayne Crichlow
item.content:encoded: Barts is one of many UK institutions whose benefactors were involved in the trafficking of enslaved AfricansInside the Great Hall of St Bartholomew’s North Wing, alongside stately portraits of the apostle from whom London’s oldest hospital takes its name and King Henry VIII, extravagant commemorative boards adorn the walls.The Great Hall was a grand, formal space where governors weighed their philanthropic donations and drafted their wills, many while investing in the stock of companies built on the trafficking of enslaved Africans. Today, many of those donors are commemorated in acrylic gold paint on the boards.Continue reading...

item.title: Africa’s richest man aiming to make $23bn from continent’s biggest-ever IPO
item.author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan and agencies
item.content:encoded: Public offering of Aliko Dangote’s Nigerian oil refinery business could swell his net wealth by two-thirdsThe fortune of Africa’s richest person could swell by two thirds to nearly $60bn (£44bn) after his refinery in Nigeria listed publicly in the continent’s biggest-ever initial public offering.If Monday’s flotation of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals on the Nigerian exchange goes to plan, then Aliko Dangote will add a further $23bn (£17bn) to his $35bn net worth.Continue reading...

item.title: Indonesian police investigate deaths of Australian man and two children in Bali as suspected murder-suicide
item.author: Caitlin Cassidy
item.content:encoded: Police in Bali believe the two young children died as a result of violence, while a 57-year-old man is believed to have taken his own life Indonesian police are investigating the deaths of three Australians who died in Bali over the weekend, with initial reports suggesting a father killed his two young children before taking his own life.The man, 57, and his two children, seven and four, who are also Indonesian citizens, were discovered deceased in a bungalow in Kuta on Sunday morning.Continue reading...

item.title: At least six dead and 130 missing after Indonesian ferry capsizes, officials say
item.author: Jon Henley and agencies
item.content:encoded: Search and rescue agency says 107 people brought to safety from vessel hit by bad weather in Java SeaRescue workers in Indonesia said at least six people had died and 130 others were missing on Sunday after a ferry sailing between the islands of Java and Borneo capsized in bad weather.Basarnas, Indonesia’s national search and rescue agency, said 107 people had been rescued from the Virgo ⁠Transport 8 vessel, which set sail on Saturday with 243 ​people onboard, including 30 crew members, ​from ‌the East Java ‌city of Surabaya.Continue reading...

item.title: One dead and more than 30 missing after ferry sinks off Vanuatu coast in rough seas
item.author: Guardian staff and agencies
item.content:encoded: Prime minister’s office tells families of those missing ‘the nation stands with you’ as search and rescue efforts continueOne person has died and more than 30 are missing after a ferry sank off the coast of Vanuatu, the country’s government says.The vessel, MV Matui, had set sail with more than 40 passengers and crew on Friday from the island of Santo to Ambae island in very rough seas, but did not arrive.Continue reading...

item.title: Burial of King Oyo takes place in Uganda as news anchor prepares for throne
item.author: Reuters in Kampala
item.content:encoded: Royal guards carry casket through streets of Fort Portal amid row over appointment of Edward Rukidi KijanangomaUganda’s King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, long the world’s youngest monarch, has been buried among the tombs of his royal forebears as ⁠his Tooro kingdom looked to put ⁠a bitter succession battle behind ​it.Oyo’s appointed successor, the news anchor Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, cast nine coffee berries into the grave at the Karambi Royal Tombs, marking the formal handover of power in the western Ugandan kingdom.Continue reading...
